body:
From the pre-release security review of the server's network interface
(2026-07-26). Post-1.8.1.

## Problem

auth.validate_email has no length bound at all, and neither does the password
path or device_label. This is in contrast to invites.py:17
(MAX_INVITED_EMAIL_LENGTH = 254) right next door, and to the thorough per-field
caps throughout sync.py (T-85). Measured:

    register with 100,000-char email    -> 201   (stored: 100,012 chars)
    register with 500,000-char password -> 201

A ~4 MB email is storable (MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH is the only bound), and it is then
echoed to every co-member via GET /lists/<id>/members and to every admin via GET
/admin/users — so one account bloats other users' responses.

device_label is likewise uncapped and untyped (the type half is covered by the
type-confusion ticket).

Separately, EMAIL_RE = ^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$ accepts ':'. Since mint()
rejects colons in invited_email, an account whose address contains one can never
be invited to any list — a silent, permanent dead end.

## Fix

- Cap the password at 320 bytes (user's call; no RFC governs this, and scrypt
  has no short input limit, so this is purely an anti-bloat bound). 422 over cap.
- Cap the email. RECOMMENDATION: 254, not 320 — see the note below; user
  proposed 320 and should make the final call at implementation time.
- Reject ':' in email addresses in validate_email, so registration and
  change-email can never create an un-inviteable account.
- Cap device_label (a UI-supplied device name; the sync engine's
  UPDATED_BY_MAX_LENGTH = 128 is a reasonable precedent).
- Apply all of it to BOTH register and account/change-email — change_email
  currently calls validate_email only, so it inherits every gap above.

## Note on 254 vs 320 (user asked for this to be double-checked)

Both numbers are real, but they are different kinds of limit:

- RFC 5321 §4.5.3.1.1 / §4.5.3.1.2 cap the PARTS: local-part 64 octets, domain
  255 octets. 64 + 1 + 255 = 320. This is what RFC 3696 §3 describes, and where
  the 320 figure comes from.
- RFC 5321 §4.5.3.1.3 caps the WHOLE: "the maximum total length of a
  reverse-path or forward-path is 256 octets (including the punctuation and
  element separators)". The path is <addr>, so the address itself is 254.

320 is therefore not simultaneously achievable — an address that long cannot
appear in a RCPT TO path and is not deliverable. 254 is the practical maximum,
which is what invites.py:17 already uses and cites.

Concrete consequence of choosing 320 here: registration would accept addresses
in the 255..320 range that mint() then rejects, so those accounts could never be
invited to a list. If 320 is chosen anyway, MAX_INVITED_EMAIL_LENGTH must be
raised to match, or the mismatch becomes a real functional bug.

## Verification

Boundary tests at cap and cap+1 for email and password, on both register and
change-email; a test that a colon-bearing address is rejected at registration.
title: accounts: no length cap on email/password/device_label; reject ':' in email addresses
